title: Declare a motion budget and honour it
intent: Make motion an amount stated before the build and checked afterwards, not a taste improvised during it.
when_to_use: the brief calls for an expressive page and motion is part of the intended experience
a reduced motion path can ship in the same pass as the animation
when_not_to_use: the surface is a tool where motion competes with input latency
the team cannot ship a reduced motion path in this release, in which case the budget is zero
rules: the contract motion dial and the artifact agree: a dial above 2 requires at least one real animated transition, and a dial at 1 forbids them
every animation is accompanied by a reduced motion rule that removes it
animated properties are limited to transform and opacity; width, height, top, and left are never animated
no animation is driven by a scroll event listener
at most one marquee exists on a page, it pauses on hover and on focus, and its content is readable without it moving
trade_off: A stated budget caps expressiveness and turns over performance into a visible defect rather than a flourish, so a page that would have been dressed up stays plain.
failure_mode: The dial is written into the contract to look ambitious while the page ships static, which is a declared claim the artifact never delivers.

example.brief: Product tour page, brief asks for a lively feel.
example.ruling: Motion dial 3, realised as three entrance transitions on transform and opacity, each wrapped in a reduced motion rule, and the contract records the three so the check can compare the claim with the artifact.
